case_title.reason: Title matches the judgment heading 'Jamnadas v. State of M.P.'

number_of_accused.quote: charge-sheet was filed against four accused namely - Manoj ... Vishal
number_of_accused.reason: Four accused were charged; three convicted. The value 3 omits the four charged and the acquittal.

accused_gender.reason: Accused include male (Jamnadas, Manoj, Vishal) and female (Dhanwantari) persons.

accused_age.reason: No ages of accused are stated in the judgment.

accused_religion.reason: Religion of accused is not mentioned.

accused_caste.reason: Caste of accused is not mentioned.

accused_occupation.correct_value: Businessman (Jamnadas only, who ran a shop)
accused_occupation.quote: appellant Jamnadas is a businessman having his shop at 5/2, Murai Mohalla
accused_occupation.reason: Only Jamnadas is described as a businessman; the value applies it to all accused.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: Socioeconomic status of accused is not stated.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No previous criminal record is mentioned.

victim_gender.reason: Victim is a young bride, referred to as female throughout.

victim_age.reason: Victim's age is not stated; only described as a young bride.

accused_victim_relationship.reason: Accused are husband and in-laws (father-in-law, mother-in-law) of the deceased.

offence_category.reason: Offence is murder of the deceased bride.

statutory_provisions.reason: Charges were under ss.302/34, 201, 304-B and 498-A IPC as listed.

weapon.correct_value: Knives and scissors (examined by forensic lab); hard and sharp object per autopsy
weapon.quote: reports ... regarding examination made on 25-09-2006 of weapons (knives and scissors)
weapon.reason: The judgment refers to knives and scissors as weapons and a hard and sharp object.

evidence_type.correct_value: Circumstantial, medical (autopsy), recovery (blood stains, Activa seized), eyewitness (PW 1-5), forensic (blood on nails)
evidence_type.quote: PW I to PW 5 who was seen doing so
evidence_type.reason: No dying declaration appears in the judgment; eyewitness and forensic nail evidence are omitted.

confession.reason: No confession by accused is mentioned; they gave false s.313 explanations.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: Body cut into pieces, blood stains, false explanation and multiple perpetrators are all noted by the court.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: The judgment does not discuss any mitigating circumstances.

trial_court_outcome.reason: Trial court convicted three accused and acquitted brother-in-law Vishal.

high_court_outcome.reason: High Court dismissed the appeals, affirming convictions.

final_outcome.reason: Supreme Court dismissed the appeals, so convictions stand.

offence_finally_established.reason: Court held common intention murder under s.302 read with s.34 IPC established.

imprisonment_type.reason: Trial court sentenced each convict to life imprisonment under s.302/34.

imprisonment_years.reason: Sentence is life imprisonment, with no fixed number of years stated.

fine_rs.quote: pay fine of Rs.5000/- ... in default of payment ... one year
fine_rs.reason: Judgment states a fine of Rs.5000 was imposed on each convict under s.302/34.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Neutral facts without stating the court's conclusion that the chain was complete or the defence was false
neutral_facts.quote: The prosecution established a complete chain of circumstances linking the accused to the crime.
neutral_facts.reason: Facts reveal the court's outcome, stating the chain was complete and the defence was proven false.

offence_severity.correct_value: Life imprisonment under s.302/34 IPC as sentenced
offence_severity.quote: sentenced each of the convicts under Section 302/34 IPC imprisonment for life
offence_severity.reason: The judgment states no statutory minimum or 'death' range; the minimum is not supported.

attempt_completion.reason: Murder was completed; the deceased was killed and body disposed of.

physical_harm.reason: Autopsy records multiple ante-mortem and post-mortem injuries and death from multiple injuries.

number_of_offences.correct_value: Two offences of conviction: s.302/34 IPC (all three) and s.201 IPC (Dhanwantari only); ss.304-B and 498-A acquitted
number_of_offences.quote: On other heads, the accused stood acquitted from the charge.
number_of_offences.reason: Value conflates accused with offences; convictions were under s.302/34 and s.201 only.

financial_property_loss.reason: Judgment does not discuss property or financial loss; 'Not applicable' is an inference, not stated.

premeditation_planning.quote: had common intention with the co-accused (mother-in-law) in the commission of brutal murder
premeditation_planning.reason: Court found common intention only; premeditation or planning is never stated.

motive.reason: No motive for the murder is identified in the judgment.

key_evidence_accepted.reason: Court relied on the chain including blood stains, body disposal, and false s.313 explanation.

witness_credibility.correct_value: Court accepted PW 1-5 sighting and medical evidence; no explicit credibility assessment; PW 32 declared hostile
witness_credibility.quote: PW I to PW 5 ... were seen doing so
witness_credibility.reason: Judgment does not expressly assess credibility; it omits that PW 32 was declared hostile.

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: No police report lodged about the homicidal death; false explanation given under s.313 Cr.P.C.
post_offence_conduct.quote: There is no report lodged to police by the appellants regarding homicidal death
post_offence_conduct.reason: Judgment records the absence of any police report and false s.313 explanation as post-offence conduct.

custody_duration.reason: Arrest dates are given but no custody duration is stated.

trial_duration.correct_value: Offence 16.09.2006; trial sentence order 24.8.2009; High Court 23.08.2012; Supreme Court 29.06.2016
trial_duration.reason: 24.8.2009 is the sentencing order date, not the trial judgment date; conviction date not given.

legal_representation.reason: Counsel for appellants and State are listed as in the judgment.

investigation_status.reason: Charge-sheet was filed against four accused and trial was completed.

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: Defence alleged police illegally detained accused for 3 days without formal arrest; court did not address it
procedural_irregularity.quote: the police illegally detained them for 3 days without formally arresting them
procedural_irregularity.reason: Defence raised an alleged illegal detention; 'None noted' omits this claim.

appeal_history.correct_value: trial_court: Convicted under s.302/34 IPC (and s.201 for Dhanwantari); high_court: Conviction affirmed; supreme_court: Appeals dismissed
appeal_history.quote: the trial court found rest of the three accused ... guilty
appeal_history.reason: Trial court entry wrongly says conviction was affirmed; the trial court convicted.

prosecution_argument.correct_value: State relied on Suresh for s.106 burden and on the chain of circumstances
prosecution_argument.quote: learned counsel for the State of Madhya Pradesh has referred to the case of Suresh
prosecution_argument.reason: Summary largely restates court findings; State's actual argument (reliance on Suresh for s.106) is not captured.

defence_argument.correct_value: Defence said deceased went missing after visiting relative, appellants were in shop, and no adverse inference from silence (Selvi)
defence_argument.quote: reliance is placed on paragraph 141 of Selvi
defence_argument.reason: Final sentence reverses the defence claim; it was that the deceased was missing. Silence argument omitted.

legal_principle_applied.reason: Five Sharad Sarda circumstantial-evidence principles are accurately summarised.

precedent_relied_upon.correct_value: Relied on: Sharad Sarda (1984), Trimukh Maroti Kirkan (2006), Suresh (2015), Kuldeep Singh (2000), Rumi Bora Dutta (2013); referred to: Mir Mohammad Omar (2000), Nafendra Singh (2004)
precedent_relied_upon.quote: Kuldeep Singh and others v. State of Rajasthan ... relied on
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Omits Kuldeep Singh and Rumi Bora Dutta, which the court relied on; Mir Mohammad Omar and Nafendra Singh were only referred to.

sentencing_rationale.reason: Judgment gives conviction reasoning but no sentencing rationale for the life sentence.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: Judgment does not state the court found no mitigating factors; 'None' is an unsupported assertion.

judicial_aggravating_factors.correct_value: Brutal murder of a bride within six months of marriage; body cut into pieces
judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: a young bride was brutally murdered within six months of her marriage, her body chopped off in two pieces
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Court describes the murder as brutal and the body as cut in two, which are aggravating characterisations.

other_sentence_order.correct_value: Dhanwantari: 3 years rigorous imprisonment and Rs.5,000 fine under s.201 IPC (default 3 months RI)
other_sentence_order.quote: Convict Dhanvantari was further sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of three years
other_sentence_order.reason: Judgment records a separate s.201 sentence for Dhanwantari, not 'None'.
